transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess… things have just been harder at home lately. My sister and her baby moved back in, and since then I’ve been kind of on edge. I get irritated over dumb little stuff, and then I go to class or the shop already feeling worn out.

I’m still managing, mostly, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines, and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, like activities you usually like doing?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I haven’t paid that much attention to it. I still like the same stuff, it’s just been harder to make time for it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Not most of the day, nearly every day, no. I mean… I’ve been more down than usual since my sister and the baby moved back in, and kind of drained. But it’s more like I’m on edge and worn out from everything at home, not just depressed all day every day.
Have you found that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in things as you used to, even things you normally enjoy?
I’m not sure. I mean, I still like the things I usually like… I just haven’t really been doing much of them lately. I don’t think it’s that they stopped being enjoyable.
Have you noticed that you're not getting as much interest or pleasure out of things as you normally would, even if you still like them?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really noticed it like that. I still like things, I just haven’t been doing much.
Have you found that, even when you do get to do things you normally enjoy, like [specific activity], you don’t get as much pleasure or interest out of them as you used to?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big difference when I actually do something I like… it’s more that I don’t get around to it much.
Even when you do get to do things you normally enjoy, do you find that you take less pleasure or interest in them than you used to?
Not really... I mean, I haven’t noticed that. If I actually do something I like, it’s still okay. I just don’t do it as much.
Even when you do get to do things you normally enjoy, do you find that you take less pleasure or interest in them than you used to?
Yeah… I mean, I think I already said, not really. If I actually do something I like, it’s fine enough. I just haven’t paid that much attention to it.
Have you felt a constant sense of worry or tension lately, even when nothing specific is happening?

Yeah… kind of. Since my sister and her baby moved back home, the house just feels more tense, and I’ve been more on edge even when nothing’s really happening. I’m still doing what I need to, mostly, but I show up to class or the shop already worn out.
Even when you're not busy or stressed, do you find that you don't look forward to or get as much interest or pleasure out of things as you used to?
I don’t think so. I mean… when I actually do something I like, I can still get into it. I just maybe haven’t been thinking about it much.
Even when things aren't stressful or busy, do you find that you’re less interested or get less pleasure from things you normally enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean… I don’t think I’m enjoying things less. I just haven’t really been paying attention to that, I guess.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, even during times when things aren’t particularly stressful or busy?
No… I don’t think I’ve noticed that. If I’m doing something I normally like, it’s still fine. I just haven’t really been focused on it much.
Have you noticed that, even during times when things aren’t stressful or busy, you still feel less interest or enjoyment in activities that you normally like to do?
Not really. I mean, I’ve kind of answered that… I haven’t noticed that happening. If I’m actually doing something I like, it’s still okay.
Even when things aren’t stressful or busy, do you find that you have to push yourself to get interested in or enjoy things you usually like doing?
I don’t think so. Like… if I decide to do something, I can usually get into it. I just maybe haven’t been doing much of that lately.
Even when things aren’t stressful or busy, do you find that you have to push yourself to get interested in or enjoy things you usually like doing?
No… I don’t think so. I feel like I already kind of said it, but if I’m doing something I like, I don’t really have to force it.
Even when things aren't particularly stressful or busy, do you find that you feel less motivated or less excited about things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or activities?
Not really, no. I mean… I haven’t noticed that when things are calm. If I actually start doing something I like, it’s usually fine.
Even small things that you might usually look forward to, like seeing a friend or finishing a project, do you find that you don’t get as excited about them ahead of time?
I don’t think so… I mean, I still look forward to stuff like that. Maybe not in a huge way, but I wouldn’t say I don’t get excited.
Even when you're not doing anything in particular and things are calm, do you find that you don’t feel much pleasure or interest in things around you?
Not really. If things are calm, I don’t usually feel, like… empty or uninterested. I just kind of do whatever I’m doing.
Even small positive things that might happen, like getting a compliment or finishing something you’re working on, do you find that you don’t feel much when those things happen anymore?
No, I don’t think so. Like, if I finish something or someone says something nice, I still feel… good about it, I guess. I haven’t noticed that being gone.
Even when something good is going to happen, like a plan with friends or finishing something you’re working on, do you find that you don’t feel much excitement or anticipation ahead of time?
I mean… not really. I still look forward to things if I know they’re coming up. Maybe I’m not super hyped, but I wouldn’t say I don’t feel anything ahead of time.
